rundown: Scotland beat Australia 15-12 at Scottish Gas Murrayfield in Edinburgh, Scotland. It was level at 0-0 at the half.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 15, 10:07 AM ET. It had Australia 39% and Scotland 61%, projecting Australia 28.3 – Scotland 32.6 (60.9 total, Scotland by 4.3).

Final: Australia 12 – Scotland 15. Right winner: it had Scotland at 61%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Australia came in with a 10% above average attack and a 12% leakier than average defense (LLLWT, 34 scored and 32.5 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 11 and 11 games of evidence. Projected to score 28.3, they scored 12 (−16.3 points, 58% under); projected to allow 32.6, they allowed 15 (−17.6 points, 54% under).

Scotland came in with a 8% above average attack and a 14% leakier than average defense (LWLWL, 32.3 scored and 35 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 11 and 11 games of evidence. Projected to score 32.6, they scored 15 (−17.6 points, 54% under); projected to allow 28.3, they allowed 12 (−16.3 points, 58% under).

The bigger miss was Scotland's scoring (-17.6 points against projection); both sides underscored their projections, so the game ran colder than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 27 against 60.9 projected (-33.9), about the 1st percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±15).

Margin: Scotland by 3 against Scotland by 4.3 projected, about the 47th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±16).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.448 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by -1.3 points. It counts toward Rugby scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Rugby learning switches on at 20 graded games (19 so far).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total outside its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
